title: 1. Origin, Corporate Evolution & Past Stock Cycles

epigraph.quote: Separating decision making from actuation is not merely an architectural slogan; it is the engineering wedge that lets software replace mechanical complexity.
epigraph.author: Engineering principle behind the SEDEMAC acronym, IIT Bombay SINE (2007)

web_blocks.html: SEDEMAC Mechatronics Ltd began in 2007 inside SINE at IIT Bombay [2, 12]. Prof. Shashikanth Suryanarayanan co-founded the firm with students Pushkaraj Joshi, Amit Dixit, and Manish Sharma. Its name reflects one clear control thesis: Separating Decision Making from Actuation [2, 12]. Older small engines relied on physical sensors, linkages, and discrete relays for timing and load control. SEDEMAC replaced those parts with compact electronic control units (ECUs) running custom software algorithms. That shift cut hardware cost while lifting reliability [2, 7].

The company's first decade was a study in patient product-market discovery rather than instant hypergrowth. In its early years, SEDEMAC operated as an R&D-heavy engineering lab. It was backed by Nexus Venture Partners, the India Innovation Fund, and the NRJN Family Trust [2, 6]. Instead of chasing passenger-car Tier-1 contracts dominated by global incumbents, management targeted an overlooked niche around 2012–2013: Automatic Mains Failure (AMF) and governing controllers for diesel and gas generator sets [8]. By delivering rugged, software-driven controllers tailored to Indian grid instability, SEDEMAC built a cash-generating beachhead. Over time, it captured roughly 75% of the domestic Indian genset controller market [8].

The decisive inflection arrived in 2018. SEDEMAC commercialized its proprietary Sensorless Commutation (SLC) Integrated Starter Generator (ISG) technology at scale with anchor customer TVS Motor Company [7, 13]. Traditional two-wheeler engines relied on a separate starter motor, Bendix gear, and mechanical one-way clutch to crank. Brushless conversions also required Hall-effect position sensors. SEDEMAC's patented algorithms eliminated both the starter motor and the physical rotor-position sensors. They used the existing wet magneto as both starter and alternator [7, 10, 11]. India's shift from carburetors to BS-VI Electronic Fuel Injection (EFI) in 2020 and OBD Stage II-B diagnostics accelerated adoption. As a result, SEDEMAC's revenue compounded from ₹240 Cr in FY21 to ₹1,058 Cr by FY26 [1, 4, 15].

web_blocks.title: Cap-Table & Corporate Milestones (2007–2026)
paragraphs: Over nearly two decades, SEDEMAC's cap table evolved from academic incubation at IIT Bombay SINE (2007) through early venture rounds (Nexus Venture Partners, India Innovation Fund, NRJN Family Trust) and growth-stage private equity (Iron Pillar, A91 Partners, Xponentia/360 ONE) [2, 6].

The company filed its Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) with SEBI in November 2025 and its Red Herring Prospectus (RHP) on February 25, 2026, completing its public listing on March 11, 2026 [6]. Crucially, the ₹1,087.45 Cr IPO (80.43 lakh shares) was structured as a 100% Offer for Sale (OFS) with zero fresh issue proceeds flowing to SEDEMAC's balance sheet. Post-listing shareholding as of September 2026 shows Promoters holding 26.23% (with zero share encumbrance declared for FY26), DIIs 38.34%, FIIs 10.30% (up from 2.52% in March 2026), and Public 25.12% [1].

Post-Lock-Up Supply Overhang & ESOP Dilution: Following the 6-month pre-IPO lock-in expiry on September 10, 2026, institutional holders including A91 Emerging Fund, Xponentia Opportunities Fund, and HDFC Life Insurance offloaded roughly 10% equity (~44.3–48.79 lakh shares) via block deals on September 24, 2026 subject to a 60-day lock-in on further sales, creating recurring supply overhang into late November 2026. Separately, SEDEMAC received NSE/BSE in-principle approvals for ESOP pools totaling ~9.75 lakh shares (~2.2% potential dilution) under ESOP Scheme 2025 (October 2026), 1.47 lakh shares under ESOP 2014 (June 2026), and 1.215 lakh shares on November 13, 2026.

web_blocks.takeaway: SEDEMAC's operating history shows a classic deep-tech J-curve: 11 years from 2007 founding to 2018 ISG commercialization, followed by two distinct margin regimes—semiconductor-era compression (10–11% OPM in FY22–FY23) and scale-driven expansion (18–20% OPM in FY25–FY26) [1, 7].

web_blocks.html: Examining SEDEMAC's operating cycles reveals two critical lessons about its business rhythm. First, revenue growth has never been smooth or linear: it surged 49% in FY23, moderated to 25% and 24% in FY24–FY25, and then accelerated 61% in FY26 and 41% YoY in H1 FY27 as new vehicle platforms and regulatory mandates layered on top of existing programs [1, 5]. Second, operating margins remain sensitive to global electronic component cycles. During the FY22–FY23 semiconductor crunch, OPM dipped to 10–11%, and in H1 FY27, printed circuit board (PCB) and memory/chip inflation trimmed quarterly OPM from 21% back to 19% despite 40%+ top-line growth [1, 5].

book_paragraphs: If you want to understand SEDEMAC Mechatronics, you have to start in a mechanical engineering laboratory at IIT Bombay in 2007, not on a factory floor in Pune. Most Indian auto-component companies begin as build-to-print metal benders or wiring-harness assemblers that license foreign blueprints and compete on labor arbitrage. SEDEMAC began with the exact opposite DNA. Prof. Shashikanth Suryanarayanan and three of his students—Pushkaraj Joshi, Amit Dixit, and Manish Sharma—incubated the company inside IIT Bombay's SINE with a thesis encoded directly into its acronym: Separating Decision Making from Actuation.

Think about what that phrase means in plain English. Inside a two-wheeler engine or a diesel generator, dozens of mechanical parts and physical sensors exist solely to tell the machine where a shaft is positioned or when to fire a spark. Those sensors sit in hot, oil-soaked, vibrating environments where they fail, add wiring, and drive up bill-of-materials cost. SEDEMAC's founders bet that if you move the intelligence into high-speed embedded control algorithms—reading tiny electrical ripples inside the motor or alternator windings themselves—you can eliminate the physical sensors and mechanical starters altogether.

Now, you and I both know that deep-tech lab theses rarely pay the bills in year one. Between 2007 and 2017, SEDEMAC spent a full decade in the wilderness of product-market fit, sustained by patient venture capital from Nexus Venture Partners, the India Innovation Fund, and the NRJN Family Trust. Their first real commercial breakthrough did not even happen in automotive mobility; it happened around 2012–2013 in stationary power generation. India's erratic grid meant every commercial building, telecom tower, and factory ran backup diesel gensets, and SEDEMAC built Automatic Mains Failure (AMF) controllers that were smarter, tougher, and more locally supported than imported European boxes. That industrial beachhead eventually gave them roughly 75% of the domestic Indian genset controller market and kept the lights on while they perfected their automotive control stack.

The true inflection point arrived in 2018. Working closely with TVS Motor Company, SEDEMAC commercialized its patented Sensorless Integrated Starter Generator (ISG) on mass-market Indian two-wheelers. By turning the engine's existing wet magneto into both a silent starter motor and a power generator—without adding a single Hall-effect sensor inside the crankcase—SEDEMAC handed OEMs a cleaner, quieter, fuel-saving micro-hybrid architecture just as India's BS-VI emission norms (2020) and OBD Stage II-B mandates forced every two-wheeler off carburetors and onto Electronic Fuel Injection.

Look at what happened to the operating cycle once those two engines—regulatory mandates and sensorless ISG adoption—locked together. Revenue rose from ₹240 crore in FY21 to ₹283 crore in FY22, ₹423 crore in FY23, ₹531 crore in FY24, ₹658 crore in FY25, and ₹1,058 crore in FY26, before reaching ₹1,265 crore on a trailing twelve-month basis through September 2026. Along the way, growth-stage investors including Iron Pillar, A91 Partners, and Xponentia joined the cap table, culminating in the company's February 2026 Red Herring Prospectus and March 11, 2026 public listing. Importantly, the ₹1,087.45 crore IPO was a 100% Offer for Sale with zero fresh capital flowing to SEDEMAC—which left the company relying on internal accruals, leases, and debt for its H1 FY27 factory expansion—while post-lock-up institutional exits (including a ~10% equity block sale in September 2026 by A91, Xponentia, and HDFC Life with a 60-day lock-in expiring in late November 2026) and active ESOP grants (~2.2% potential dilution under ESOP Scheme 2025) remain ongoing cap-table factors.

Yet the operating history also carries a warning label that you should not gloss over. SEDEMAC's margin cycle is tied to silicon and PCB supply chains. In FY22 and FY23, when global semiconductor shortages spiked component costs, operating margins compressed to 10% and 11%. By FY26, scale pushed operating margins to 20%, only for PCB and chip inflation in H1 FY27 to nudge them back down to 19%. This is an IP-led business, yes—but it is also a physical electronics manufacturer living inside global component cycles.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Eleven years elapsed between SEDEMAC's 2007 founding at IIT Bombay and its 2018 ISG commercialization with TVS Motor. That long gestation explains both its moat—competitors cannot replicate a decade of embedded control-theory iteration overnight—and its structural vulnerability, because scaling a deep-tech product in India required hitching its wagon to one anchor OEM.

book_subsections.title: Why the Cap Table and Margin Regimes Matter for What Comes Next
paragraphs: When you trace SEDEMAC's cap table from 2007 to 2026, you see both institutional pedigree and a classic post-IPO supply transition. Early venture backers—Nexus Venture Partners, the India Innovation Fund, and the NRJN Family Trust—absorbed the long R&D gestation years, followed by Iron Pillar, A91 Partners, and Xponentia ahead of the March 11, 2026 listing. Because the ₹1,087.45 crore IPO was a 100% Offer for Sale with zero fresh issue proceeds to the company, SEDEMAC did not receive an IPO cash cushion to fund MF3 and MF5. Meanwhile, promoters hold a steady 26.23% with zero encumbrance, while pre-IPO investors began monetizing after the September 10, 2026 six-month lock-in expiry—led by a roughly 10% equity block sale on September 24, 2026 by A91, Xponentia, and HDFC Life subject to a 60-day lock-in, alongside ~9.75 lakh ESOP Scheme 2025 shares (~2.2% potential dilution) cleared by exchanges in October and November 2026.

That institutional backing gave SEDEMAC the patience to survive two very different margin regimes. During the FY22–FY23 global semiconductor shortage, revenue still grew from ₹283 crore to ₹423 crore, but operating margins compressed to 10%–11% as chip prices spiked and interest costs climbed to ₹16 crore in FY23 and ₹38 crore in FY24. Once supply normalized and ISG volumes crossed critical mass in FY25 and FY26, operating leverage snapped back dramatically: operating margins expanded to 18% and 20%, and net profit leaped from ₹6 crore in FY24 to ₹47 crore in FY25 and ₹104 crore in FY26. Remembering both halves of that cycle—the compression and the expansion—keeps you grounded when evaluating any single quarter's margin print.
